chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman al-Minqari, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mahdi, from al-Mubarak, from al-Aflah, who said:

I asked Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) about the sparrow that nests in the house, are its chicks taken? He said, 'No, for the chick, while in its nest, is in God's guarantee as long as it has not flown. And if a man hunted in its nest and hit the bird and the chicks all together, he would eat the bird but not the chicks, because the chick is not considered game as long as it has not flown, and it is only taken by hand, and it only becomes game when it flies.'
ai.seo_question: Are baby birds in the nest considered game and permissible to eat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Sajjad (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between adult birds and their nestlings, establishing that chicks remain in God's guarantee (dhimmah) and are not yet considered 'game' until they fly. It provides a practical legal criterion for consumption, noting that if an adult is hunted and accidentally kills the nestlings, only the adult is consumed, reflecting the principle that the young are not yet independent prey. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precise definitions of ownership and divine guarantee in dietary laws.
